subject: Human Evolution
title: Freeing the Hands
description: A short lesson to help you apply Freeing the Hands.

hook.text: Walk on two legs and your hands are suddenly free. That accident changed everything.

buildup.text: Free hands could carry food, babies, and tools—advantages no knuckle-walker could match.

discovery.text: Darwin proposed this idea in 1871: tools drove bipedalism. But bipedalism predates tools by millions of years.

twist.text: Carrying food to share may have been the real driver—cooperation, not tools, freed those hands first.

climax.text: Free hands became tool-using hands, which became writing hands. All because we stopped using them to walk.

punchline.text: Two feet gave us ten free fingers.

quiz.question: What did bipedalism allow that quadrupedalism didn't?
options: Free hands for carrying and tools
